review_notes: I read the whole file. I compared the three-way case split (Multipliable, NeBot, finprod fallback) in tprod_le_of_prod_le', one_le_tprod, tprod_le_one and tprod_nonneg. I also compared the filter argument in prod_le_hasProd and prod_le_hasProd_of_nonneg. I checked Defs.lean for tprod_bot and tprod_eq_one_of_not_multipliable, and checked the finset lemma prod_le_one in Algebra/Order/BigOperators/Group/Finset.lean. Only the tprod_le_one duplication seems to justify a change. one_le_tprod and tprod_nonneg have no dual upper-bound lemma to reuse, and a generic helper for their case split would just move the branches. The prod_le_hasProd and prod_le_hasProd_of_nonneg overlap is two lines, so I did not report it. I could not compile the proposed replacement, so it is untested.

findings.problem: tprod_le_one redoes the whole case analysis (Multipliable or not, L.NeBot or not, finprod fallback) that tprod_le_of_prod_le' (lines 148-158) already carries out for an upper bound a₂ with 1 ≤ a₂. Its statement is the special case a₂ = 1 of that lemma. The only extra ingredient it needs is that every finite product of terms ≤ 1 is ≤ 1. The file proves that again in the non-NeBot branch via finprod_induction instead of using the existing bound. So the NeBot split and the tprod_eq_one_of_not_multipliable fallback are proved twice.
findings.proposed_change: Prove it from the existing lemma. Take the general lemma tprod_le_of_prod_le' with a₂ = 1 (so 1 ≤ 1 is le_rfl). For the finite-product hypothesis use the finset lemma prod_le_one (the additive form is sum_nonpos). The body becomes: `tprod_le_of_prod_le' le_rfl fun _ ↦ prod_le_one fun i _ ↦ h i`. The hypotheses are available: the section has IsOrderedMonoid, and OrderClosedTopology gives ClosedIicTopology. tprod_le_of_prod_le' is already declared earlier with `omit [IsOrderedMonoid α]`, so no new imports or instances are needed. If the finset lemma has different instance requirements, a one-line `prod_le_one'`-style fallback by induction on the finset would also work.
findings.benefit: The Multipliable/NeBot/finprod case split is written once for upper bounds, and tprod_le_one shrinks from about nine lines to one. Any future change to how the non-NeBot and non-multipliable cases are handled only needs to be made in one place. A reader also sees that tprod_le_one is the a₂ = 1 case of tprod_le_of_prod_le'.
